S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account and available unit/model identifiers. They must provide affected customers with a safety notice within 72 hours, and promptly update it as facts are confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%. A model exceeding 5% must submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retest within 12 months. While the plan is being implemented, sales may continue unless the regulator finds an imminent safety risk or the manufacturer fails to meet the plan.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units sold from 24 months after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For installed units, manufacturers must submit a regulator-approved, risk-based retrofit plan within 24 months after adoption and complete any required retrofit within 72 months, prioritizing higher-risk units.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance protocol. Regulators may grant only time-limited, publicly documented exceptions where equivalent protection is demonstrated.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate a regulator-supervised recall, including repair, replacement, or refund options and progress updates. A recall is a corrective safety action, not an automatic market ban; regulators may impose additional restrictions where necessary to address an imminent risk.

document.section_notes: The final S1 is strong: all thermal incidents must be reported within 24 hours and customers notified within 72 hours, which covers both companies' unreported incidents. S2 keeps the 5% limit and blocks public per-model publication, but lets models above 5% keep selling indefinitely during a corrective plan, which favours Northwind's 6.2% Hearth 10. S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 24 months and sets a 72-month retrofit, which favours Northwind's 38% shut-off coverage, while S5 imposes a mandatory recall at 8 per 100k with no transition, which bears on Halcyon's 9.9 Ember 8.
